newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar black market rate stable at 3.8 to mark.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar black market rate stable at 3.8 to mark.

text.p: The Yugoslav dinar black market exchange rate remained stable at 3.8 to the German mark over the weekend after plunging to 4.3 in the week of January 6.
"There is no change compared to the past few days and no significant trade in either direction," a street dealer told Reuters.
On Monday, dealers were buying marks for 3.8 and selling them for 4.0 dinars.
Another dealer said the dinar dropped to 4.0 at Belgrade's main flea market on Sunday but did not reflect the general trend in the capital.

"There is a shortage of dinars at the moment," the same dealer said but added fresh cash was expected to hit the streets later in the week when pensions were due to be paid to around 1.5 million pensioners in Serbia.

Some analysts attributed the plunge to growing inflationary expectations and fears of devaluation, while others said it was caused by an increase in money supply to ensure payment of overdue wages and pensions before Orthodox Christmas and New Year holidays.
In its 1997 economic policy, the Yugoslav government has vowed to keep the currency stable at 3.3 to the mark.

The dinar was devalued by 70 percent in November 1995 to bring it in line with the then black market rate. Its street value remained stable at 3.4-3.5 until last November after devaluation fears mounted before general elections.

Independent analysts linked the latest dinar plunge to the political crisis in Serbia following the annulment of local election results which stripped the opposition of victories in most major towns. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
